title: Yannick Bolasie close to Middlesbrough loan switch from Everton
trail: Everton winger Yannick Bolasie would link up with his old manager, Tony Pulis, in a loan move to Middlesbrough
body: Everton’s Yannick Bolasie is close to joining the Championship leaders, Middlesbrough, on a season-long loan and could soon be followed by his Goodison Park teammate Mo Besic. Bolasie travelled on Monday to Rockliffe Park, Middlesbrough’s training ground near Darlington, for talks with Tony Pulis, Boro’s manager, and for a medical. The 29-year-old Democratic Republic of the Congo winger cost Everton £25m two years ago but injuries disrupted his progress last season and he is surplus to Marco Silva’s plans. Bolasie had hoped for a permanent move to a Premier League club – Crystal Palace, his former club, and Burnley both expressed interest – but the transfer window closed before any deal could be completed. Football League clubs are free to take players on loan from Premier League or overseas teams until the end of the month, facilitating Boro’s pursuit of Bolasie. Discussions between the two parties are said to be advanced, with the eventual deal possibly containing a clause triggering a £15m permanent transfer should the Teesside club win promotion, but matters have been complicated over how Boro and Everton split Bolasie’s £70,000-a-week wages. Money proved the stumbling block to Besic joining Boro for around £6m on deadline day but the Bosnian midfielder, a successful loanee at the Riverside last season, is expected to return on another short-term deal. Bolasie played under Pulis, albeit briefly, at Selhurst Park and their mooted reunion would represent a statement of Boro’s promotion ambitions at the end of a summer in which they have sold three key players in Patrick Bamford (to Leeds), Ben Gibson (Burnley) and Adama Traoré (Wolves) for a collective £45m. Bolasie’s likely switch will represent a blow to Steve Bruce, Aston Villa’s manager, who had also been hoping to borrow a winger capable of operating on both flanks. Pulis, despite his team’s strong start, has persistently reiterated the need to strengthen his squad through judicious use of the loan market and remains in pursuit of a left-back, with Southampton’s Matt Targett his principal target.
